html:
VKF 0.2.1 — Exact Output Proof And Faster Native Kernels

VKF 0.2.1 fixes two native-code correctness gaps found while strengthening the release proof, then optimizes the same compact vector-pipe forms used by the language guide and Fannkuch benchmark. It adds no runtime dependency.

Correctness

  • Consecutive compound updates inside a function preserve an established fixed-vector type when an intermediate expression is otherwise inferred as any. The 10-million-operation container example now returns its required 10000000 result instead of silently reusing one vector element.
  • macOS ARM64 indexed fixed-vector loads and stores now convert native integer locals through the numeric value ABI. Integer bits are no longer reinterpreted as floating-point values in range-pipe assignments.
  • The documented-program verifier checks committed exact stdout for the two high-value regression examples as well as repeated-run byte stability. A consistently wrong output can no longer pass merely because it is stable.

Native Optimizer

  • Indexed assignments whose onward result is immediately discarded bypass the temporary value round trip introduced by pipe lowering.
  • Fall-through-only continuation labels are removed before backend pattern recognition.
  • Compact fixed-vector copy and bounded-shift pipes recover dedicated integer lowering without requiring manual counter loops.
  • Proven two-pointer prefix reversals retain both indices in registers across the loop and write them back only on exit. Their source-level temporary is committed once per reversal rather than once per swap.
  • Scalar fields in structured locals, such as result.checksum, are now eligible for integer registers. Only storage proven to be indexed stays memory-backed. This makes compact structured code fast without flattening it into unrelated variables.
  • Proven constant indices in unrolled small-vector interaction kernels use direct frame addresses instead of reconstructing indexed addresses.
  • Statically unrolled three-component interactions keep adjacent x and y lanes packed through subtraction, dot products, velocity updates, and stores; z remains scalar. This reduces N-body work without changing its numerical result.
  • The policy tuner seeds interaction-heavy small-vector programs with a safe policy selected by the exhaustive landscape for that program shape, then validates it against the scalar result. When no tuning budget remains, it falls back to the conservative validated policy instead of unvalidated aggressive code.
  • Fannkuch declares its exact int -> int contract. The committed release comparison is regenerated from the final compiler and is the authoritative performance result.

Verification

  • The native suite contains 333 passing VKF tests.
  • Every documented program is compiled and executed 10 times on Windows x64, Linux x64, and macOS ARM64 with exact output checks.
  • The controlled Linux comparison performs 100 fresh compilations and 1,000 raw runs for spectral norm, Fannkuch, and N-body. Each fresh VKF compilation receives an 80 ms optimizer-search budget, and the complete search remains included in reported VKF compile time.
  • Final raw VKF means are 4.719 ± 0.125 ms for spectral norm, 24.131 ± 0.301 ms for Fannkuch, and 4.488 ± 0.261 ms for N-body. Every same-host VKF/C, VKF/Rust, and VKF/Zig ratio is below 2×; the largest is N-body versus Rust at 1.904×.
  • physics, ui, and symbolic remain excluded rather than shipping partial or compatibility implementations.

The installed compiler continues to emit PE, ELF, or Mach-O executables directly. Compiling and running VKF requires no Python, C++ compiler, assembler, or separate linker.
